##### **Improvements to your** **_Copper Monitor_** 

##### Dear Subscriber, 

We are pleased to present to you your improved _Copper Monitor_ . In line with CRU’s LME metal portfolio, this service now incorporates a number of enhancements to the **quality** and **consistency** of data and presentation of content.

September 2012 Copper Monitor www.crugroup.com #### Market seeks direction In quiet trading conditions, LME copper prices continue to be dominated by macro-economic developments. Bouts of optimism over the likelihood that fresh government stimulus measures will be forthcoming and drive copper demand higher have been countered by spells of pessimism following the release of disappointing economic data which points to a further deterioration in the world’s major economies. Under these two opposing influences, LME copper prices have remained largely rangebound, lacking sufficient impetus to break out decisively on the upside or the downside. Since the beginning of August, the LME 3-month price has traded between $7,300-7,700/t; a range that is almost $100/t lower than that which prevailed in July. A further sign that the market has softened in recent weeks is the persistence of a contango. Between 1st -29th August, a cash to 3-month contango was recorded on 95% of trading days compared with just 59% in July. Despite depressed market conditions, LME copper prices did rally briefly in the second half of August following a US Federal Reserve meeting in which it was suggested that further monetary stimulus measures were likely. But the upturn, which lifted the LME 3-month price to a 5-week high of $7,676/t on August 23rd , was q

uickly reversed as concerns re-surfaced over the eurozone financial crisis and in particular the likelihood that Spain will need a bail-out. At present, attention is focussed on the forthcoming meeting of the US Federal Reserve Price stabilises and contango

Until there is more clarity over the global economic outlook, it is unlikely that copper prices will embark on a determinedly upward or downward trend. In fact, it has not just been LME prices that have been range-bound. SHFE and COMEX copper prices have also traded sideways for much of August, though quotes have moved higher more recently. #### Funds on the fence The lack of any conviction surrounding the likely Data: LME short-term direction of prices continues to discourage investors from taking up sizeable new positions in copper. Futures open interest on the LME has consequently declined further, recently hitting a five and a half year low. In the current environment, any investors that do enter the market are more likely to be net short than net long. This is supported by the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report which shows that non-commercial traders using the COMEX copper contract have become increasingly net short. Moreover, there is limited confidence that spot Data: Comex, CFTC, LME, *weekly to 22<sup>nd</sup> May 2012 demand for copper will pick-up significantly in September and October, especially in view of recent economic data.  The latest composite leading indicators (CLI) from the OECD point to a continued slowdown in economic activity in Europe and signs of fading growth momentum in the USA. 

The Chinese market is also not faring much better.  China’s CLI contracted further in June and growth in industrial production was particularly disappointing in July, as it dropped to 9.2% y-o-y from 9.5% in June.  Additionally, the flash PMI for August registered its lowest reading since last November. However, with inflation falling to a two and a half year low, further policy easing remains a possibility. 

#### Demand weak in China... 

Chinese copper demand has been subdued in August.  To a large extent, this is not a surprise.  Consumers are in no hurry to re-stock as inventories held by the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) together with the bonded warehouse stocks in Shanghai and Nanhai are high and rising.  Purchasing behaviour consequently remains very much hand-to-mouth.  Of greater concern is the growing realisation that even if buying activity does improve in September, and we assume a similar monthly stock drawdown rate to last year, it could take more than 6 months for the existing volume of stock (740,000t) to be reduced to levels considered normal (300,000-350,000t). 

Visible copper stocks in SHFE warehouses plus those held in the bonded warehouses in Shanghai and Nanhai are estimated to have totalled 740,000t at end-August, compared with a peak of 779,000t in April. Moreover, stocks of copper, having been drawn down in the second quarter, have risen again in the last two months.  SHFE stocks fell to 139,400t at end-June but subsequently rose to 156,510t by end-July and have edged higher to 158,900t in August. Inventories held in non-SHFE bonded warehouses in Shanghai and Nanhai have also increased in the last two months, up by 127,000t to reach 581,000t by end-August.

#### ...but imports strong and production is rising 

The increase in Chinese copper inventories is not just a reflection of weak spot demand; imports have also been high.  In July, Chinese imports of refined copper totalled 254,339t, a 31% y-o-y increase although volumes were flat m-o-m.  Given the large quantity of imported copper earlier this year and the weak state of current buying activity, many industry participants were expecting Chinese imports to drop sharply in July.  The fact that they have been maintained at above 250,000t suggests material is either being imported under long-term contract or is required for financing purposes or both. 

Meanwhile, Chinese exports fell again m-o-m in July but

are still running at elevated levels. At 12,500t, much of the material continues to be exported to South Korea. Recent changes in export taxes (3% export tax on cathode has been lifted for the seven large smelters that are allowed to export on a tolling basis, while 17% VAT is now applied to TC/RCs for imported concentrate) have made it more attractive for some smelters to export cathode. For the time being though, the LME/SHFE arbitrage is not wide enough to encourage significant export growth. Easy availability of copper in China has also been exacerbated by a solid increase in domestic production. CNI-A has reported that refined cathode output totalled 3.2m tonnes in the first seven months of the year, up 8.9% y-o-y. 1.1Mt of scrap have been consumed in cathode production to date but smelters are now reported to be having difficulty sourcing additional secondary units. As a result, some facilities have been forced to cut output since June or close for maintenance work. Given the reduction in scrap supplies, Chinese refined copper output could well be flat or even fall slightly during the remainder of the year. The combination of ample availability of copper coupled with lacklustre Chinese demand led to a reduction in spot cathode import premiums in August. Quotes now fall in a range of $55-$60/t, cif Shanghai, down from $70-$80/t reported last month. The premium for SXEW material is currently being quoted at $40-50/t, down slightly from a prior range of $40-$55/t. #### European and US spot demand sluggish There has been no change in market conditions in Europe and the USA. Though the summer holiday season is coming to an end, spot demand remains weak in both regions and early indications of likely levels of demand for September suggest no major change. Of course, volumes are likely to increase for © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 4 of 19 September 2012 Copper Monitor www. crugroup.com seasonal reasons but producers and traders indicate there are no signs that consumers will require any additional quantities over and above the seasonal uptick. More positively, inventories in Europe are low while those in the USA remain modest. In Europe, LME stocks totalled just 15,851t on August 29, having fallen slightly in August. Given the weakness of demand, it is perhaps surprising that inventories have not increased and some commentators are concerned that volumes may rise in September. In the USA, the total quantity of stock (LME plus COMEX) is much higher at 167,000t and although invento

ries have increased a notch in August, they remain well down on year-ago levels. While any revival in spot demand could result in tighter European and US markets, any tightness is likely to be temporary as ample stocks exist elsewhere, notably in Asia. The continued lack of spot business makes it difficult to accurately assess merchant premiums. Overall, European premiums are believed to have edged down to $55-75/t, cif Rotterdam, compared with $60-80/t last month. In the USA, premiums are reported to have softened by 0.5¢/lb and are quoted at 6.5-7.5¢/lb, delivered east coast. Rumours that material normally destined for Europe has been diverted to the USA, with potentially negative implications for premiums, are unsubstantiated. #### Economic clarity needed to change status quo In the absence of further stimulus measures, LME copper prices appear set to remain range-bound. At the top end of the range, any upward movement in price is clearly being restricted by weak demand and the release of poor economic data. At the lower end, prices are being supported by hope that additional stimulus measures will eventually emerge and by recent underperformance of copper supply. The lack of growth in refined copper production in the first half of the year is a key reason behind our view that the market was in deficit to the tune of 146,000t. Disruptions at several existing operations plus delays to new mines restricted the increase in refined output to just 1.2% y-o-y in the first six months. Interestingly, there have been limited reports of disruptions and delays to mine production so far in the third quarter. In addition, there are over 25 new mines scheduled to start-up in the second half. Despite this, the market remains unconvinced that supply is set to accelerate. BHP Billiton’s recent announcement that it will shelve the expansion at its Olympic Dam facility has added credence to the view that copper production will continue to struggle, leaving the market tending towards deficit. Our own estimates support this view with the copper market expected to experience a deficit of 124,000t in the second half. Market still tending towards

#### Copper tube A faltering outlook on Chinese demand, in situ with the ongoing Eurozone debt crisis, has continued to depress the global copper tube market. Global copper tube consumption has declined by 4.5% y-o-y to 623,000t in Q2 2012. This represents a 5.1% increase from Q1 2012, however, we attribute this to a typical seasonal uptick in consumption. Regionally, China, the biggest producer and consumer of copper tube, witnessed flat copper tube production in **450** Q2 2012 compared to the same period last year, in spite **400** of an uncertain economic outlook. Copper tube **Q109 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q110 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q111 Q2 Q3 Q4 Q112 Q2** production contracted by just 0.5% in Q2 2012 y-o-y to **Data: CRU** 281,000t, with consumption up by 1.2% y-o-y to 249,000t. On a quarterly basis, production increased by 9.8% in Q1 2012 q-o-q, aided by a seasonal uptick in demand. For a more detailed look at the Chinese copper tube market, please refer to the next section. With respect to new Chinese production, in mid-June, **Hengyuan Copper Co. Ltd.** , based in Shandong province, began commercial production of a newly installed 20,000t/y copper tube line. The company invested RMB380M in the line. Meanwhile, **Zhengteng Group** , based in Guangdong province, announced that it will begin construction of a 150,000t/y copper products project in H2 2012. The operation will produce oxygen-free copper wirerod, copper busbars, tubes and wires beginning in H2 2012 from a facility located in Yushan County, Shangrao City in Jiangxi province. It remains uncertain what portion of the total production will be accounted for by copper tube. Investment capital for the project is expected to total RMB 1.5B. Uncertainties over Chinese demand have caused negative production growth in the remainder of Asia. In particular, Q2 2012 output in South Korea tumbled by 14.39% y-o-y. Other Asian countries are specifically affected by demand in the rest of the world. A case in point would be Vietnam, which exports upwards of 50% its copper tube output to the US. In recent years, much copper semis production has been off-shored from China to Vietnam in order to cut costs and often to circumvent trade restrictions. For example, most recently, the International Trade Administration (ITA) ruled in mid- August that imports of copper tube from China to the US between 22nd November and 31st October were sold below normal value. As a result, Chinese exporters are being hit by increasingly stringent anti-dumping regulations, which can be avoided by exporting from other Asian nations. In North America, copper tube production experienced a seasonal rebound, with production in the US growing by 11.1% q-o-q to 70,900t on promising growth in the construction sector. Regardless, the Q2 2012 output level is still lagging behind production in the same period last year, down by 5.1% y-o-y. Tube

**Mueller** , stated in its Q2 2012 report that the US tube market faced a difficult trading period, causing the company to suffer lower net sales to the plumbing and refrigeration segment due to slightly lower spreads. Mueller also reported that its sales to original equipment manufacturers of plumbing brass; automotive components; valves and fittings; and specialty tubing, valves and assemblies for the refrigeration, airconditioning, gas appliance, and barbecue grill markets were down due to lower unit sales and a squeeze on the company’s margin.  The construction market in the USA continues to show signs of some improvement, however the overhang of empty houses and homeowners with negative equity on their mortgages in the residential segment means that overall construction activity growth will be uneven at best. 

In other news, US production is facing the threat of a strike at Mueller Copper Tube’s operations.  Over 250 unionised workers have rejected a collective labour contract with the company in late August.  Negotiations are currently underway, with a decision set to be made by the beginning of November 2012. 

Meanwhile, in South and Central America the copper semis market has taken a turn for the worse.  According to Sindicel, a Brazilian copper producer association, the nation’s copper semis industry has cut 3% of its workforce.  The cause of this has been attributed to slowing economic growth and increasingly competitive semis markets.  Nevertheless, we estimate that copper tube production in South and Central America increased 4.0% y-o-y in Q2 2012. 

The picture in Western Europe remains fairly bleak, with production down by 4.0% y-o-y. **KME** reports that the tube market in the region faces challenges from the Eurozone debt crisis sapping consumer and business confidence.  As a result, tube consumption and production remains under pressure, with demand from home appliance and air conditioning end users stagnant at best and other industrial sectors showing modest growth. Geographically, the market remains in a north/south divide. Northern nations are registering better consumption than southern nations, benefitting from better performing construction sectors and increased government investment into infrastructure.  Meanwhile, the situation in Eastern Europe appears much more stable, with production up by 0.7% y-o-y. 

#### Subdued Chinese demand more evident 

As we discussed in our main editorial, it is apparent within and without the market that Chinese cathode demand remained weak in August.  With semis producers facing a situation of high inventory levels of semifabricated copper, consumption has been sluggish, and so despite reduced domestic cathode output due to a number of smelter maintenance closures in Q2, cathode stock levels have increased while imports were flat month-on-month in July, due to lon

g term contractual orders and possibly financing demand. The fact that imports had maintained levels seen in June came as a surprise to some, as according to anecdotal evidence within the industry, a trend for refined copper shipments bound for the EU and China being diverted to North America has emerged in the last month or two. Underpinning the weakening in Chinese demand, and therefore the stock-build right across the supply chain, has been the palpably cooling economy. After its faltering steps in early 2012, hopes rose in Q2 of a resurgent China, led by improved indicators and falling stock levels. The latest Markit/HSBC China purchasing manager’s index for August slid back to 47.8, from 49.3 in July, marking the weakest result seen in 9 months, and the Chinese government has recently reduced its growth target for 2012 down to 7.5%, from 8%. Against such a background, subdued demand for copper semis is a logical outcome. In our previous copper tube and alloy RBS consumption trend report, found in the June edition of the Copper Monitor, we reported that a build-up in home appliance stocks was beginning to appear. If anything, the surplus in white goods has increased, and the impact has now managed to work its way upstream to the extent that copper tube producers were driven to reduce operating rates in July. According to data released by China’s National Bureau of Statistics, the production of air conditioning units increased by 26% in Q2 compared to Q1, and the production of refrigerators was up by 8% quarter-on-quarter. This was driven by anticipation that air conditioner and refrigerator unit consumption would increase in summer, and copper tube production also rose to meet demand from these sectors. CRU estimates that tube production in China increased quarter-on-quarter by 9.8% in Q2 to around 281,000t, and as the accompanying chart shows, we estimate that consumption also increased, though by the lesser amount of an 8.9% q-o-q increase to around 249,000t. The increases in both semis and end-use products also reflected efforts to meet half-year production targets within companies. However, domestic demand for these types of cooling goods was lower than hoped, and with the export market c

ontinuing to be very weak, particularly in Europe, stocks of air conditioners and refrigerators began to build. This, added to the fact that July is already a quiet period in the season for consumption, meant that copper tube stocks remained high and demand slumped, leading to the tube producers’ move to slash output. Chinese alloy RBS production is also estimated to have increased in Q2, by 5.6% to around 204,000t, while consumption increased more slowly to around 225,000t, from 211,000t in the previous quarter. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 19 September 2012 Copper Monitor www. crugroup.com ### Industry News #### Consumption - **General Cable** reported a rise in sales volume by metal weight of 2% q-o-q (+5% y-o-y) in Q2 2012 due to demand in France and the Mediterranean as well as stable demand in most ROW and North American businesses. Bright spots for demand included: ongoing grid investment in France; stronger demand from North American electric utility businesses; improving domestic conditions in Thailand after the Q3/4 2011 severe flooding; and strong mining activity in Chile. - **KME Group** , a European producer of copper rolled products and tubes, announced that company revenues (excluding the cost of raw materials) fell by 11% y-o-y to reach €376M. KME mainly attributes the decline to weak macroeconomic conditions caused by the European sovereign debt crisis which began in H2 2011. Copper price volatility has also led to cautious buying of copper products. The company said that it experienced a continued downturn in sales within the industrial sector (approximately 75% of revenue) in Italy and Spain in H1 2012, while France held up better. Sales contracted period-on-period and year-on-year in the brass rods segment and in rolled products for the construction market. In addition, shipments to domestic appliance and air conditioner manufacturers were stagnant y-o-y in H1. A bright spot was seen in sales of automotive and mechanical components as well as products associated with the electrical industry. - **Mueller Industries** , a leading producer of copper tubes and brass products, reported net sales of $594.1M in Q2 2012. After accounting for changes of metals prices, this represents a decline of 1% y-o-y. The contraction was partially offset by a slightly higher sales volume y-o-y. - **Eastern Copper** , a copper wirerod producer based in Shandong Province, announced that it has recently commissioned its second continuous copper wire rod plant. The plant will be able to produce 320,000t/y of high quality copper wirerod at full capacity. - Rolled copper production in Japan decreased by 5.7% in July y-o-y according to the Japan Copper and Brass Association. The fall

was attributed to the global economic slowdown which is pushing downward pressure on demand. Seasonally adjusted July output reached 77,764t, up by 9% from June. 



- **Russia Copper Corp. (RCC)** , a Russia-based integrated producer of copper cathode and wirerod, said that there will be a steep rise in exports of copper cathode from 2015.  The company expects Russia to cancel its 10% (variable on copper price) export duty on copper cathodes from 2015 as a prerequisite for its accession to the World Trade Organisation.  RCC added that the cost incurred in producing wirerod is around $130/t and the average cost to send it abroad in Q1 2012 was $250/t, whereas the estimated cost of sending cathode abroad was $850/t in that period.

- **Aurubis AG** reported that its production of copper wirerod was down by 22% y-o-y and 14% q- o-q to reach 155,000t in Q2 2012, marking a faster decline from the 17% y-o-y fall in Q1 2012. The company said that the decrease in volumes was driven by slower demand from cable and enamelled wire producers.  This came despite stronger demand from the automotive sector and signs of a pick-up in demand from the infrastructure sector in late Q2.  Aurubis also produces copper and copper-alloy shapes, pre-rolled products, finished flat rolled products and speciality wire.  Output of shapes fell by 25% y-o-y and 13% q-o-q to reach 41,000t in Q2, due to weak demand from semi-fabricators. However at **Schwermetall** , the company’s 50%-owned subsidiary, production of pre-rolled strip decreased by only 5% y-o-y to reach 49,000t in Q2, as demand from semi-fabricators for this product held-up better.  The y-o-y change in finished flat rolled products output was distorted by the acquisition of **Luvata** ’s rolled products division. However, volumes in the division did fall by 5% q-o-q reaching 57,000t in Q2, contributing towards across-the-board sequential declines for Aurubis’ copper products output in Q2. 

#### Mine Production 



- On 23<sup>rd</sup> August, **Anglo American** and **Codelco** announced that they had reached a settlement to end a 10-month dispute over Codelco’s use of an option contract in an attempt to acquire **Anglo American Sur** .  Anglo American will retain control of AA Sur with a reduced, 50.1% shareholding after selling 25.4% of its interest in the company to a new Codelco controlled Codelco- **Mitsui & Co** . joint venture company.  The joint venture will acquire a 29.5% shareholding in AA Sur for US$2.8B after a 4.1% share is transacted away from Mitsubishi subject to clearance by Brazilian competition authorities, reducing Mitsubishi’s holding in AA Sur to 20.4%.  Mitsubishi will receive US$890M of the total payment plus a fee of US$40M from Anglo American. 



- Operations at the **Philex Mining** ’s **Padcal** Mine in the Philippines were halted on 1<sup>st</sup> August after heavy

rains caused the mine’s tailing pond to overflow, threatening to contaminate one of the country’s largest rivers.  The spill has been contained although the extent of the environmental damages has yet to be determined.  Operations at the mine have been suspended pending an investigation into the accident and the safety of the tailings dam.  The Padcal mine was expected to produce 17,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2012. 



- **Antamina** , one of the biggest copper mines in the world, is facing opposition from local communities and a government investigation following a recent pipeline rupture that has raised environmental concerns.  On 25<sup>th</sup> July, the pipeline which transports wet concentrate from Antamina’s mine site in the Peruvian Andes to the filtration and port facilities leaked 3 tonnes of material into the surrounding area.  Local villagers who had volunteered their help in order to prevent the spillage reaching an important local water source later suffered from a range of ailments.  A government investigation is now under way and the operator **Minera Antamina** faces a fine of at least 2M soles (~US$769,000) from the regional government of Ancash.  The

#### Exploration and Development 



- The Peruvian government announced on the 28<sup>th</sup> August that it had suspended **Newmont Mining** ’s **Conga** project.  The development is attributed to a report suggesting significant changes in the company’s water supply strategy for the project.  The government added that Newmont now has two years to conceive of a way to guarantee the supply of water to local residents.  Newmont has stated that in the meantime it will continue with construction of water reservoirs to serve the local communities.  The miner had previously hoped to begin production at the mine by early 2015, producing up to 235Mt/y of copper ore. 



- On 23<sup>rd</sup> August, **Sagittarius Mines** , a subsidiary of **Xstrata** , warned that the start-up of the **Tampakan** project in the Philippines may be delayed due to regulatory and security concerns. The government refused to grant environmental clearance to the company, which is likely to result in a delay to the scheduled construction start date in 2013.  The copper-gold ore body is situated in a province that has been protected by a mining ban since 2010 and which can only be lifted by a court order.  In addition, security concerns have slowed Sagittarius’ field activities following the death of a security guard after a shooting at the site in June, which came only one month after a similar incident resulting in injuries to a guard.  The project is due to start up in 2016 at a total inve

stment cost of US$5.9B. 



- On 22<sup>nd</sup> August, **BHP Billiton** announced that it does not plan to approve any spending on major projects this fiscal year.  This means that a total of US$68B of planned project expenditure will be re-evaluated.  The company said that it will scale back its US$20B planned investment in the expansion of the **Olympic Dam** mine, adding that the project team size will be reduced from 190 to 50 people as the company seeks a smaller alternative for the expansion.  This decision follows the announcement of disappointing company results for the second half of FY2011-2012 with profit decreasing 58% from last year’s levels. 



- On 23<sup>rd</sup> August, **Pan Pacific Copper** said that its **Caserones** mine project was on track for operational start-up in 2013.  Cathode production (capacity of 30,000t/y) will commence in January 2013 and concentrate output will follow in September (capacity of 150,000t/y).  The entire copper concentrate production volume from Caserones will be treated at PPC’s Saganoseki smelter in Japan, reducing the company’s market-sourced concentrate requirement from 80% to roughly 50% of its total usage.  Once underway this operation will represent PPC’s fourth copper mine stake, all of which are in Chile.  Caserones has a slated mine life of 28 years. 



- It was reported on 8<sup>th</sup> August that **Mopani Copper Mines** had been granted environmental permits to proceed with the development of a US$8.3M open pit mine in Kitwe, Zambia.  The

#### Smelting and Refining 



- It was confirmed on 14<sup>th</sup> August that **PASAR** restarted operations of its smelter in **Leyte** , the Philippines, in July following a shutdown due to a fire in January.  It has been rumoured that there are investment plans to expand the smelter’s production capacity above its current level of 215,000t/y.  Given that the operation was closed for the entire H1 2012, CRU expects full year copper cathode production at the facility to amount to 80,000t. 



- On 21<sup>st</sup> August, China’s **Zhangjianggang United Copper** said that it will double the refined copper production capacity of its **Jinfeng** , Jiangsu province smelter by the end of 2013.  The company intends to invest RMB1.53B to lift capacity to 400,000t/y.  Construction will begin by December 2012. 



- **Yunnan Tin Ltd.** announced on 28<sup>th</sup> Aug

ust that its 100,000t/y electrolytic copper processing plant has entered into a trial phase, with a current monthly production of 1,500t.  Complete startup is expected in H2 2012 and the company forecasts annual production in 2013 could reach 90,000t. Total investment expenditure on the project amounted to RMB1.99B.
